The ST and its ancillary plant and equipment shall provide continuous, safe, reliable and economical operation without undue heating, vibration, or noise. It shall be located indoors and designed for ease of operation and maintenance and shall have rapid start-up and shutdown capability. Appropriate concepts shall be included in the design so as to minimise blade erosion due to exhaust steam wetness.
An exhaust hood spray cooling shall be supplied, if necessary, to limit the exhaust temperature rise under conditions of low exhaust flow operation.
The ST shall incorporate an interface with the DCMS to facilitate integrated control of the Plant throughout all operational manoeuvres.
The ST shall also be capable of coming to rest without any damage on loss of cooling and/or main AC power to its oil systems.
The control system shall include features to provide automatic intervention to limit maximum thermal stress levels to established threshold values.
The steam turbine unit and all auxiliary plant shall be provided with all equipment necessary to monitor all significant operational data.
The HP steam header shall feed two identical condensing steam turbine-generator units. Each steam turbine shall be fitted with a steam extraction to feed the FGP.
Overloading requirements specified in IEC60045 shall be taken into account. The turbine main valves shall be of the fail-safe type.
On-load testing of emergency stop valves and of the simulated over-speed trip gear operation shall be possible.
All fleet wide modifications in design and construction recommended by the ST manufacturer after award of the Contract up to Plant final takeover shall be immediately informed to the Owner and the Contractor shall implement the same free of cost and without any time impact to the Owner. The details of modifications, schedule and mode of implementation shall be mutually discussed and agreed upon with the Owner.
All the latest upgrades/improvements/safety modifications announced by the manufacturer (TIL/ECN etc.) before and during the contract period up to Plant final take over shall also be applicable for this contract and implemented by the Contractor free of cost and without any time impact to the Owner at shop or at site with the consent of owner.

Heat recovery steam generator (HRSG) shall be complete with ducting, chimneys, mountings, integral valves and pipes and all other items associated with the unit to allow reliable operation.
The HRSGs shall be of proven design and in accordance with the requirements of relevant ASME standards where applicable or equivalent international standard. The HRSG shall be ASME stamped. The HRSGs shall incorporate supplementary firing for meeting the steam requirements as set forth in Exhibit B, Part 1. HRSG shall be entirely suitable for the exhaust gas temperatures and mass flow rates of the gas turbine resulting after supplementary firing (at full load and all required loads and ambient conditions).
The HRSGs and all associated facilities (e.g. Gas supply system, steam supply system etc.) shall therefore be capable of accommodating the following operating cases:
- continuous operation of HRSG without supplementary firing
- continuous operation of HRSG with minimum supplementary firing enabling fast increase of steam generation
- within design limits operation of supplementary firing according to steam demand by steam generation control or by steam pressure control; continuous operation of HRSG with maximum supplementary firing
The HRSG shall be designed for cold end corrosion issues and so that exhaust gas temperature is above the acid dew point when the gas turbine is fired on Gas.
Inspection doors and platforms shall be provided to allow ready access to the HRSG gas path, tubing and other pressure parts.
Gas duct linings and insulation shall use materials with proven capability at the maximum gas temperatures anticipated, together with design margin to allow for uneven temperature distribution downstream of supplementary firing burners. The duct geometry downstream of the supplementary firing burners shall be designed so as to ensure that no direct flame impingement on heat exchange surfaces or other metallic surfaces can occur.
The pinch point for the HRSGs shall be optimised at the design point and shall be less than 36 0 F (20 0 C).
The HRSGs shall be designed for outdoor installation and all equipment and mountings shall be entirely weather-proof and suitable for the aggressive environment. The main pressure parts shall be arranged in the form of a self-contained construction and shall be of the self-draining, horizontal gas pass type.
The water side of the HRSG shall be chemical/acid cleaned after completion of erection in accordance with accepted chemical cleaning procedures.
Regarding HRSG pressure retaining parts material selection shall be in line with requirements and stipulations of ASME I (pressure vessels) and ASME B31.1 (power piping).
All fleet wide modifications in design and construction recommended by the HRSG manufacturer after award of the Contract up to Plant final takeover shall be immediately informed to the Owner and the Contractor shall implement the same free of cost and without any time impact to the Owner. The details of modifications, schedule and mode of implementation shall be mutually discussed and agreed upon with the Owner.

Contractor shall provide correction curves for gross power output of the Steam turbine versus ambient conditions of dry bulb temperature and relative humidity. In addition, the ACC shall be capable of handling steam turbine bypass operation during start-up, shut-down and/or emergencies (shall include a reserve of at least 10% to cover possible steam turbine overloads). The orientation and layout of the ACC shall be such that the adequate air circulation is possible around the ACC.
Each ACC fan shall be individually isolatable. Access ways, galleries, platforms and ladders shall be provided for safe and efficient operation and maintenance including maintenance of fans, gearboxes, bearings etc. The ACC shall comprise a number of cells mounted on a hot dip galvanised steel support structure. Internal partition walls shall be located between each fan section to reduce mal-distribution of air flow. Lockable access doors shall be provided in the partition walls (normally kept closed and locked).
The ACC shall be of proven design with supplier references demonstrating the same. The ACC shall be designed for full vacuum to an approved heat exchanger design code as applicable such as Heat Exchanger Institute (HEI) Standards for Steam Surface Condensers, ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code etc.
The ACC shall be of the forced draught type, located on a steel structure at ground level. It shall be capable of condensing steam from the steam turbine and turbine drain flash vessel (if provided) at all ambient conditions and at all loads.
The ACC shall be arranged to minimise the recirculation of cooling air.
During steam turbine trip transient/start-up phase, the whole steam flow from the by-pass system will be discharged to the ACC.
During the by-pass conditions, the ACC shall be able to maintain the pressure such that no limitation occurs for the steam turbine capabilities.
In addition to the requirements of Exhibit B, Part 1; the ACC shall be designed to be capable of condensing the entire steam flow dumped by the by pass system following a steam turbine trip, for indefinite time.
Finned tubed bundles shall be used within the ACC. The tube fin material combination shall be of Welded carbon steel tube + carbon steel fins (both hot dipped galvanized). In case Contractor proposes Aluminium coated (Aluminized steel) tubing with Aluminium fins then the same is acceptable only for single row type condensers.
Wind walls shall be installed around the perimeter of the ACC structure, minimally extending from fan deck level to the top of the heat exchanger bundles. Each ACC shall be equipped with systems such as high pressure spray to enable cleaning of the outer surfaces of the tubes.
Fans shall be of single-speed type. The Contractor shall develop the operating concept for ACC during the detailed design phase.

The Gas conditioning and filtering skid shall include carbon steel filters/separators installed downstream of Plant Gas Delivery Point. The filters/separators shall be fabricated per ASME VIII to remove solid particles of micron size 3µ with an efficiency of 100% filtrate rate and 0.5µ at 99.5% or better and liquid particles of micron size 3µ with an efficiency of 100% filtrate rate and 0.3µ at 99.5% or better, to the requirements of the gas turbine equipment supplier. Liquid drain from the filter separators shall be routed to the fuel gas condensate drain tank from where it will be truckloaded out for disposal. Level-indicating transmitters and switches shall provide level indication to the control room operator. The isolation valves for filter separators shall be double seat ball valves.
Gas pressure control stations shall be provided for each of the Plant power and steam Unit. The Gas pressure to the Plant power and steam units shall be controlled within the appropriate operating range via pneumatically operated control valves. The pressure control station shall be provided with necessary control valves. A pneumatically operated highpressure shutoff valve will also be provided to close upon high downstream Gas pressure and will minimize the amount of Gas vented to atmosphere when the safety relief valve lifts. Triple redundant pressure transmitters shall be provided downstream of the regulating station to provide a highly reliable Gas pressure control system that will minimize unnecessary turbine trips. The Gas System shall be provided with ESD valves upstream to the fuel gas system.
Extended capacity strainer shall be provided to remove impurities from the Gas. A pressure switch shall monitor the differential across the strainers will signal an alarm to the central control room via DCMS for the pressure drop across the strainer indicates cleaning is required.
If required, Gas heaters and heating water boosting pumps shall be provided in order to control Gas temperature to maintain variation of Modified Wobbe Index (MWI) within +/- 5% to enable the gas turbines to operate at full load for both the Gas qualities within the specified ranges in Exhibit B, Part 1.
Scrubbers shall be provided to remove liquid inside fuel gas. In case the gas pressure is lower than heating liquid, scrubbers will also be installed downstream to the fuel gas heaters to prevent any moisture carry over from any tube leak in fuel gas heater. Liquid drain from the scrubber shall be routed to a fuel gas scrubber condensate drain tanks from where it will be truck-loaded out for disposal.
For each gas turbine, 2 coalescent final filters (2 x 100%) shall be foreseen (if required by the gas turbine manufacturer).
Piping after last scrubber to gas turbine shall be of stainless steel, if recommended by the manufacturer.

The Plant shall be equipped with chemical dosing systems to control the boiler and Feedwater chemistry. The chemical dosing system to control the boiler and Feedwater chemistry will be operated based on chemistry parameters of HRSG water. Since the steam will be used in Saudi Aramco processing facilities, the chemical dosing agents chosen have to be agreed with Saudi Aramco. However, the following shall be considered as preliminary:
- ammonia NH3
- Oxygen scavenging chemical, only during malfunction
- trisodiumphosphate Na3 PO4
The Contractor may propose also other chemicals if he can demonstrate long term economical, successful and safe utilization in other plants. A fully automatic chemical dosing system shall be provided for ammonia and oxygen scavenging. For trisodiumphosphate, manual dosing is acceptable as long as on-line phosphate analyzer is implemented .
The operational parameters of quality of the steam leaving each HRSG shall meet the parameters specified in IEC/TS 61370. The make-up water quality shall be produced accordingly.
All chemical dosing systems shall be supplied and provided as complete systems.
Each injection shall allow the conditioning of the boiler within 30 minutes and maintain sufficient excess of the chemicals in the steam drum.
Each chemical dosing system shall comprise all equipment for the safe, reliable and efficient operation of the dosing systems, including bunds, segregated chemical drains, appropriate ventilation and emergency eye wash and deluge shower units.
Each chemical dosing system shall consist of two (2) x 100% chemical dosing pumps and one (1) chemical dosing tank.
The chemical dosing tank shall combine solution mixing and preparation and shall be made of stainless steel or synthetic material. It shall have a working capacity of 4 days of continuous use for each additive. The tank shall be provided with electric agitator as necessary.
The dosing pumps material shall be AISI 316L (1.4404) for the casing. Two (2) pumps per chemical shall be provided.
Injection pipes and valves are made of stainless steel AISI 316L (1.4404).
Bulk storage for each chemical shall be provided with a storage capacity of at least 7 days with the Plant at full load. For chemicals in liquid or gaseous state bulk storage tanks sized to unload a full standard road tanker shall be provided Plus 4 day's storage capacity. Required unloading arrangements and interconnections for auto transfer between the storage tanks and dosing tanks shall also be provided.
